_comment: Tier-2 for sparta rarefied_flow:16, executed on the installed binary (SPARTA 24 Sep 2025, spa_serial). Two decks, identical apart from the LAST argument of 'fix dr dt/reset 100 c_dtg 0.1 <resetflag>', both driving the same compute grid -> fix ave/grid -> compute lambda/grid -> compute dt/grid chain. With resetflag 0 the Dt column is constant for the whole run while f_dr still publishes a recommendation that differs from the timestep the deck set; with resetflag 1 the Dt column moves at multiples of Nevery and, on every row where it moved, equals f_dr on that same row. Both statements are relations INSIDE one run — a column being constant, and two columns of one table agreeing — so no timestep, ratio or tolerance is remembered. That the recommendation is published in both decks is what makes the pair clean: the fix does identical arithmetic either way and only the write-back differs. COVERS: rarefied_flow:16. MUTATION CONTROL (T2_MUTATE=1, re-runnable): the resetflag of the rewriting deck is set to 0 — the single edit that removes the pathology — with the compute chain, weight, Nevery, seed, timestep and run length untouched. The two decks become one deck and the Dt column stops moving. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES (rc=0); with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1) and these expect_in_output strings go False and disappear: resetflag_one_rewrites_the_global_timestep=True, the_new_dt_is_the_fixes_own_recommendation=True. The report-only assertions describe the deck the hook turns everything into, so they correctly stay True. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/sparta/dt_reset_rewrites_the_timestep && python source.py (passes, rc=0), then T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py (fails, rc=1). Needs a SPARTA binary: the fixtures find spa_serial/spa_mpi on PATH or at ~/Schreibtisch/sparta/src/spa_serial, else set SPARTA_BINARY; with none present they exit 0 on a SKIP: line, which forbid_in_output turns into a failure.
